correctness.rationale: IFR survival-ratio monotonicity gives an exact upper envelope F_s(t) for the mean at fixed tail mass and central-survival ratio. The function increases strictly in s; at the algebraic threshold the active-set derivative has no interior maximum, endpoint values decrease in the active-set index by a proved exponential inequality. The one sharp equality profile is explicitly reconstructed and has finite mean, IFR survivals and equal central point masses. Exact rational arithmetic also confirms a five-point counterexample to extending the older three-point formula; finite grid checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Direct statement/implication comparison with the recent integer-IFR mean-tail theorem: its sharp local-ratio formula is explicitly restricted to gamma<=1/2, while the ratio-one case here has a different sharp two-rate geometric extremizer. The 2024 Feige and 2020/2024 localization results require log-concave point probabilities, whereas the present equality law is IFR but violates PMF log-concavity at its two central masses. Targeted indexed research-record searches give no directly covering theorem. A historical reliability report is an uninspected residual risk, so originality remains qualified.

value.rationale: The adjacent mass ratio is an explicit mathematical parameter in the recent discrete-IFR mean-tail theorem. The gamma=1 case has a new sharp algebraic constant and an equality law of different geometry from gamma<=1/2; the classification improves the quarter guarantee and identifies where the three-point extrapolation fails. A universal and unique extremizer for an infinite class is mathematically motivated and cannot be replaced by an arbitrary finite test.
